Science is an ongoing and often slow process, and uncertainty and evolving questions are 
inherently a part of that process. The scientific method is our best approach for building our 
TYPES OF RESEARCH STUDIES AND HOW TO INTERPRET THEM
91

understanding of how the world and human life works. Many different types of studies can 
contribute to scientific knowledge. None are perfect—all have limitations—and a single study is 
never the final word on a scientific question. Part of what advances science is that researchers are 
constantly checking each other’s work, asking how it can be improved and what new questions it 
raises. And all of this moves us closer to consensus, usually built on a foundation of many different 
studies from every level of the hierarchy of evidence pyramid, and usually multiple meta-analyses of 
those studies. 
One final note: If there’s a lot of debate on a scientific question, then that probably means that 
the science is still young and messy, and there’s not enough evidence for experts to settle on a 
consensus. In this scenario, be skeptical of anyone who claims to know the absolute truth or makes 
promises that seem too good to be true. We often see such claims in the field of nutrition, where 
book authors, podcasters, celebrity influencers, and companies selling products for a profit say 
they know the secrets of good health. They’re often operating in areas of scientific uncertainty, 
extrapolating from a few interesting findings, or outside of consensus entirely.
